newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 28.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* A federal judge ruled the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had authority to regulate sales and labelling of cigarettes, in a major blow to the tobacco industry.
* Federal investigators are examining Columbia/HCA over its physician-referral methods in Miami.
* Harnischfeger announced a $631 million hostile bid for U.S. machine-tools maker Giddings & Lewis.
* European Union and U.S. trade officials have started talks about European complaints regarding U.S. subsidies to aircraft manufacturers.
* In March, existing home sales fell 2.8 percent from February as some buyers were discouraged by rising rates.
* In an expected government filing, television broadcasters say Rupert Murdoch's proposed satellite-television venture should have to require all local station signals.
* AT&T is set to hire senior Bell Canada official and deal maker Dan Somers as its new chief financial officer.
* The S&P 600 is being chosen over the Russell 2000 by some mutual-fund companies as a benchmark for their small-stock index funds.
* Some big grain companies and lawmakers are resisting CBOT plans to limit futures-contract delivery points to an area around Chicago.
* American Express's credit card operations outpaced its rivals in 1996 because it allied with other firms to target overlooked markets and it offered incentives.
* According to market research firms, the personal computer industry's growth slowed in the first quarter but still topped 15 percent worldwide.
* VLSI is set to introduce a major upgrade to its process for chip-manufacturing.
* EDS announced its first decline in quarterly profit, prompting shares to drop 23 percent.
* Westinghouse reported a larger-than-expected quarterly loss, with losses at its energy systems operation and at CBS.
* Nissan Mutual's collapse signals that Japan's financial crisis has spread to the insurance industry.
* Outboard Marine said its investment banker was reviewing the company's strategic options and that it would not declare a dividend this quarter.
* The Dow Jones industrials fell 53.38 points on Friday to close at 6,738.87.

* Heard on the Street: Why aren't the agitators taking stakes in Reader's Digest Association ? Because there's not much they can do without the nonvoting shares sold to the public seven years ago. The venerable mail-marketer of canned American culture is a perfect candidate for forced reform or a takeover.

* Credit markets: Look out U.S. bond market, you may soon have serious competition. As the countdown to European Monetary Union proceeds, bond market participants are wondering if a new single-currency European bond market capable of competing with the U.S. Treasury market will emerge.
